items.broken: Unsourced legal paragraph with no rule by passport
items.status: Fixed, one US line waits for Nic
before: "Non-residents can legally marry in Portugal, but the paperwork takes time, so start three to six months ahead. You will typically need long-form birth certificates issued within the last six months and a Certificate of No Impediment, translated into Portuguese and authenticated with an Apostille."
after: Four official steps from Portugal's civil registry: start at least one month before your date, and marry within six months of approval
Correct rules: documents in English, French or Spanish need no translation; witnesses are optional; both partners must be 18 or over
US passport: the US Embassy does not issue a CNI (the statement-of-eligibility line and USD 50 fee wait for Nic)
UK passport: no CNI needed if you live outside the UK; UK residents use the FCDO service
Australian passport: a CNI or registry certificates; the Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI; confirm which document is accepted and where it must be issued
Every rule links to its official source (Justiça, IRN, US Embassy, GOV.UK, Smartraveller)
items.note: The old paragraph was wrong on two points: the minimum notice is one month, not three to six, and a CNI is not required for everyone.
